ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Elizabeth Barrett Browning

code.originalText: Pulmonology consultation with CT of the chest and spirometry, diagnosis of bronchiectasis, and the start of airway clearance

text.paragraph: One-week review, seen the same morning by pulmonology with CT of the chest and spirometry. [S]

Ms. Barrett Browning returns one week after her first visit and was seen this morning by Dr. Ellesmere-Park of pulmonology, who reviewed her CT and spirometry. Her three sputum samples were negative for acid-fast bacilli on smear and by nucleic acid amplification, her interferon-gamma release assay and HIV test were negative, and the routine culture grew Haemophilus influenzae. She has worn a mask with visitors and is relieved to hear that tuberculosis is very unlikely. Her cough and sputum are unchanged, about four tablespoons a day, and she saw one thin streak of blood three days ago. She takes morphine solution 5 mL twice daily as before and has used no extra. She has booked her first grief session for this week. She started vitamin D. [S]

S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to her documented prescribed opium (D); tolerance and withdrawal on prescribed opioids do not count toward opioid use disorder.

list.item:
Bronchiectasis, left lower lobe and lingula (J47.9). The CT shows cylindrical bronchiectasis of the left lower lobe and lingula with bronchial wall thickening and mucus plugging, and no cavity, nodule, mass, or anomalous artery from the aorta, so there is no sequestration. Spirometry shows mild airflow obstruction (FEV1 2.02 L, 74% predicted; FEV1/FVC 0.69). Immunoglobulins are normal and Aspergillus-specific IgE is negative, so antibody deficiency and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis are excluded; the most likely cause is a severe infection years ago. Tuberculosis is very unlikely with three negative smears, a negative NAAT and a negative IGRA; the cultures, including for nontuberculous mycobacteria, will be final in six to eight weeks. Bronchiectasis Severity Index 3 (mild). Dr. Ellesmere-Park and I agree the plan. [S]
Airway clearance twice daily with the active cycle of breathing and an oscillating PEP device, taught by the respiratory physiotherapist this week.
Home exercise program.
Written exacerbation plan with amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for 14 days.
Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines to be given.
Mask no longer needed.

Long-term opioid therapy (Z79.891). Unchanged at 10 mg twice daily; no sedation. Dr. Ellesmere-Park notes that morphine damps the cough she needs to clear sputum, which is one reason to reduce slowly if she wishes, but there is no reason to change it urgently. [S]
Continue morphine solution 5 mL twice daily.
Naloxone at home.

Prolonged grief disorder (F43.81). First grief therapy session this week. No suicidal ideation; safety plan in place. [S]
Grief therapy weekly.
PHQ-9 at four weeks.

Follow-up: Four-week review with the mycobacterial culture progress, sputum culture, DXA, PHQ-9 and the opioid plan. Emergency care for more than a few teaspoons of blood. Next scheduled visit 2026-04-20: four-week review: mycobacterial cultures, airway clearance, bone density, grief therapy, and her choice about the opioid dose. [S]
